I am an old woman of 72 years in Mtwara, and I have been growing nuts on this small plot my whole life. I do not have money for chemical fertilizer or fancy seeds from town — I save my own seeds from last season like my mother taught me, and I mix in what little manure I get from the neighbor's goats. The rains here are what water my crop, and my children and grandchildren help me weed and harvest because my back is not strong anymore. For the hardest work I sometimes pay a young man from the village a few days to help me clear and plant.
